clue.text: Name one work (Elgar's First) after this goddess?

parts.note: to name someone is to call them
one is the Roman numeral I
OP is short for opus, a musical work

indicators.note: First points to just the opening letter of the composer's name

explanation.surface: A puzzle about naming a composition, perhaps by Elgar, in honour of some goddess.
explanation.walkthrough: Elgar invites a musical reading of 'work', which fits: OP (opus). CALLIOPE was the Muse of epic poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: Calliope is the Muse of epic poetry, one of the nine goddesses of the arts in Greek myth.

clue.text: One of Macheath's bewitching girls

parts.note: in The Beggar's Opera Macheath sings of being happy with either sweetheart were the other dear one away

explanation.surface: A captivating young woman loved by the highwayman of The Beggar's Opera.
explanation.walkthrough: Macheath, hero of John Gay's The Beggar's Opera, sings 'How happy could I be with either, were t'other dear charmer away!'
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who bewitches captivates, and Macheath's song calls each of his two loves 'dear' this word.

clue.text: Dish to toss to a Liverpudlian

parts.note: to lob something is to toss it in a high arc
a Scouse is a native of Liverpool

explanation.surface: Throwing a plate to someone from Liverpool.
explanation.walkthrough: Scouser or Scouse is the nickname for people from Liverpool, a northern English port; the stew is where the name came from.
explanation.definitionFit: Lobscouse is a sailors' stew of meat, vegetables and ship's biscuit, linked to Liverpool.

clue.text: "He's as tall a man as any's in " (T. Night)

definitions.text: "He's as tall a man as any's in " (T. Night)

parts.words: "He's as tall a man as any's in " (T. Night)
parts.note: Sir Toby Belch boasts of Sir Andrew in Twelfth Night, naming the land where the play is set

explanation.surface: A line from Twelfth Night with its last word left blank.
explanation.walkthrough: Fill the gap in Sir Toby's line: Twelfth Night is set in this Adriatic land.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare set Twelfth Night in an ancient Adriatic coastal region, and Sir Toby's line names it.

clue.text: Do this as an act of contrition

definitions.text: Do this as an act of contrition

parts.words: Do this as an act of contrition
parts.note: to make amends for sin a penitent is told to do a task, so the clue describes it

explanation.surface: An instruction to perform something as a sign of remorse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' is the verb in the phrase used for making amends: one does this.
explanation.definitionFit: A penitent performs self-punishment or prayers to show sorrow for wrongdoing.

clue.text: River origin of armadillos? Just so

explanation.surface: A natural-history note on where armadillos came from, with a nod to a children's book.
explanation.walkthrough: Kipling's Just So Stories include 'The Beginning of the Armadilloes', set on the banks of this great South American river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Amazon is South America's great river, and in Kipling's tale the first armadillos arise on its banks.

clue.text: Possessing a sense of beauty teaches it somehow

indicators.note: somehow says these letters reach the answer by some reordering

explanation.surface: A course that teaches an appreciation of beauty in some way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Somehow' rearranges TEACHES IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Being concerned with the appreciation of beauty and art is being aesthetic.

clue.text: Month intended, say, for increase

parts.note: Aug is short for August

indicators.note: say tells us the word that follows is spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: intended means meant

explanation.surface: A month set aside for growth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' makes MEANT sound like MENT.
explanation.definitionFit: To augment is to make larger, so it means to boost.

clue.text: Introduce excess fare to obtain a round figure?

definitions.text: Introduce excess fare to obtain a round figure?

parts.words: Introduce excess fare to obtain a round figure?
parts.note: fare is food, not a ticket price, and a round figure is a plump body rather than a round number

explanation.surface: Paying extra on a ticket to make the total a neat sum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Excess fare' and 'round figure' suggest train fares and tidy numbers; it is eating too much food and getting tubby.
explanation.definitionFit: Eating too much food can make a person stout.

clue.text: Their occupants may be quickly moved to attend the theatre

definitions.text: Their occupants may be quickly moved to attend the theatre

parts.words: Their occupants may be quickly moved to attend the theatre
parts.note: the theatre seems a playhouse visit, but it is the hospital operating theatre, and the occupants are patients rushed there

explanation.surface: Audience members hurried along to catch a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Theatre' suggests drama; it is the surgical operating theatre, and the speedy vehicles carry patients.
explanation.definitionFit: Emergency vehicles rush patients to hospital, where some go straight to the operating theatre for surgery.

clue.text: Miller, we hear, is Ben's lowly neighbour

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word is judged by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: ... Miller was the American big-band leader

explanation.surface: A man called Miller lives modestly beside his neighbour Ben.
explanation.walkthrough: A ben is a Scottish mountain peak, so its low-lying neighbour is a valley; Miller's first name has a double N, the answer a single one.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scotland a ben is a mountain, and the narrow valley lying below it is its lowland neighbour.

clue.text: Old dandy an important person for this course

parts.note: an eighteenth-century fop who affected Continental fashions was called a macaroni
a big cheese is an important person, so cheese alone stands for one

explanation.surface: A dated fop and some VIP are linked to a dish on the menu.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Course' is a meal course, the pasta dish; a 'macaroni' was a fashionable dandy in 1770s England.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasta baked in a sauce of melted cheddar is served as a main dish of a meal.

clue.text: A run on the Continent for singers

definitions.text: A run on the Continent for singers

parts.words: A run on the Continent for singers
parts.note: a run here is a rapid vocal flourish of notes, named with a French word, hence on the Continent

explanation.surface: A concert tour of Europe for a group of vocalists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run' looks like a tour or trip; in music it is a fast string of notes, and the term is French.
explanation.definitionFit: A vocal flourish of quickly sung notes takes its name from French, meaning a rolling ornament.

clue.text: Little boy left direction inside escritoire

indicators.note: inside says the compass point sits within the other pieces

parts.note: Dave is a short form of the boy's name David
port is the left side of a ship
N, north, is a compass direction

explanation.surface: A small boy put a direction notice inside a writing desk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inside' puts the compass point within the other two pieces; 'left' is the nautical sense, the left side of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A davenport is a small writing desk with a sloping top, a kind of escritoire.

clue.text: Law that classically divides a republic

indicators.note: divides says one piece splits the other by sitting inside it

parts.note: a republic is a state
ut is the Latin word for that, in a purpose clause, so classically means Latin

explanation.surface: A rule that, in ancient times, split a republic apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Classically' signals Latin, where 'that' (in a purpose clause) is ut; 'divides' sets it within the republic's synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: A statute is a written law enacted by a legislature.

clue.text: Final demand.A tumult I'm creating

indicators.note: creating, as in making a fuss, suggests these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A last warning: I'm making a fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Creating' rearranges A TUMULT I'M.
explanation.definitionFit: An ultimatum is a last set of terms whose rejection brings action.

clue.text: Some Turk! He diverted the old viceroy

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A Turkish official, amused, takes a diversion.
explanation.definitionFit: The khedive was the Ottoman Sultan's viceroy ruling Egypt in the nineteenth century.

clue.text: Such laughter of one who smote "is bloomin' lyre?

definitions.text: of one who smote "is bloomin' lyre

explanation.surface: A query about laughter belonging to a poet strumming a lyre.
explanation.walkthrough: Kipling wrote 'When 'Omer smote 'is bloomin' lyre', meaning the Greek poet Homer.
explanation.definitionFit: Unrestrained laughter, like that of the gods in the Iliad, and also belonging to the bard of the Iliad.

clue.text: Catch in diet arranged herein

indicators.note: in places the catch within the other letters
arranged means the letters of diet are put in a new order

parts.note: a net is used to catch fish

explanation.surface: Something caught within a diet plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arranged' scrambles the diet's letters and 'in' sets the catch within them. 'Herein' is the definition: the room where you eat.
explanation.definitionFit: A dinette is a small dining area, where meals are eaten.

clue.text: Vehicle for a child who pushes off hastily

explanation.surface: A child's ride, and a youngster who rushes away from it.
explanation.definitionFit: A child's two-wheeled push toy, and also anyone who scoots, meaning leaves in a rush.

clue.text: A German badger-hound, this dog

parts.note: the German breed whose name means badger dog has a nickname from its long, tubular shape

explanation.surface: Identifying a dog as a German badger-hunting breed.
explanation.walkthrough: The dachshund (German for 'badger dog') is popularly called a sausage dog.
explanation.definitionFit: The dachshund's long body earns it the nickname of a meat-filled tube.

clue.text: A single person emphatically feels no wrong

indicators.note: wrong means the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: A lone person feels nothing is wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrong' rearranges FEELS NO.
explanation.definitionFit: The reflexive pronoun refers emphatically to one individual, as in 'do it yourself'.

clue.text: Gives continual pain, like joints to one side of the body

parts.note: R stands for right, one side of the body
ankles are joints

explanation.surface: Pain in the joints on one side keeps coming back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To' joins: R goes beside ANKLES.
explanation.definitionFit: A grievance that rankles keeps causing bitterness or annoyance.

clue.text: Shaw's title to an island, a first-class island too!

parts.note: the Isle of Man is an island in the Irish Sea
too means also, and in addition, so 'and'
first-class means super, excellent
again the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: Shaw dedicates a play's title to an island, and to an excellent island besides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Too' supplies AND. The Isle of Man is a self-governing island between Britain and Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: George Bernard Shaw wrote the 1903 comedy of that name, drawing on Nietzsche's idea of the Übermensch.

clue.text: Lines at last for the little perisher!

parts.note: BR, British Rail, ran Britain's railway lines
taken as written

explanation.surface: Railway lines are finally put in for a naughty child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At last' places the word 'at' at the end. 'Perisher' is British slang for a pest, especially a child; the printed grid's first letter does not fit the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A badly behaved child is a brat, and British slang calls such a nuisance a little perisher.

clue.text: Decorative lantern a medical officer designed

indicators.note: designed means the letters are worked into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A doctor designs a pretty lantern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Designed' rearranges LANTERN, A and MO together.
explanation.definitionFit: Something decorative serves to adorn rather than for practical use.

clue.text: Could be grave in a manner of speaking

explanation.surface: Something might turn serious, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grave' is not solemn but the grave mark over a letter, as in à.
explanation.definitionFit: A grave mark is one type of diacritic over a letter, and a regional pronunciation is a way of talking.

clue.text: Arabian remedies insufficient for Lady Macbeth

definitions.text: Arabian remedies insufficient for Lady Macbeth

parts.words: Arabian remedies insufficient for Lady Macbeth
parts.note: Lady Macbeth says all the scents of Arabia will not sweeten her bloodstained little hand

explanation.surface: Middle Eastern cures fail to help a Shakespearean queen.
explanation.walkthrough: The allusion is Macbeth Act 5: 'All the perfumes of Arabia will not sweeten this little hand.'
explanation.definitionFit: Fragrant scents from Arabia could not mask the imagined smell of blood on Lady Macbeth's hand.
